proposed_capability: Add one welcoming Docker-backed play command with a native Windows handoff and structured failure guidance.
player_save_control_impact: Docker gets no profile, game, save, Docker socket or desktop mount. Windows only runs the established toolkit install and approved game-process dispatch. Existing running sessions are preserved, and no save selection or desktop input is admitted.
expected_outcome: One foreground player or authorized agent command builds and verifies the container startup plan, installs or reuses the toolkit, and launches a uniquely detected Windows game or preserves the already-running game. It returns the first failing stage with guidance.
negative_tests: Missing Docker and unsupported game host stop before install or launch.
A bad container plan or a failed install never calls the launch adapter.
Already-running game produces no duplicate dispatch. An ambiguous installation gives an explicit manual selection recovery.
Repeated Windows installer verification uses exact on-disk launcher bytes. No shared desktop input or automatic save action is added.
rollback_path: Revert this launcher change; legacy Start-BetterInstincts.cmd and named bootstrap.py commands offer the existing lifecycle. Existing manifest ownership and native game state remain in their original owners.
unresolved_unknowns: Windows Docker Desktop and an installed Sims 4 game are not present on the cloud worker. Actual game observation needs the Windows game host.

sprint.runtime: Linux cloud checkout; Windows Sims unavailable
sprint.collisions: Open stacked Video Gaming PRs and live BI-002 unchanged. No conflicting startup owner identified.
sprint.next_parent_gate: Container workflow and Windows game-host handoff proof
